questions.question: What makes speculative decoding acceptable in production rather than just a heuristic speed hack?
options: It exactly preserves the verifier model's output distribution
It always increases benchmark scores
It removes the need for a target model
It guarantees every drafted token is correct
questions.explanation: The lesson opens by stressing the Leviathan theorem: speculative decoding changes latency, not the verifier's sampling distribution. That exactness is why teams can enable it without accepting a quality regression.

questions.question: Which variable most strongly determines speculative-decoding speedup?
options: The tokenizer vocabulary size
The draft token acceptance rate α
The number of optimizer states saved during training
The verifier's rope_theta setting
questions.explanation: The wall-time formula depends on both the draft cost and the expected accepted tokens, but the lesson repeatedly calls α the biggest lever. Raising acceptance from mediocre to excellent draft quality nearly doubles throughput at fixed draft length.

questions.question: What two training changes define EAGLE-3 relative to earlier EAGLE versions?
options: It adds a reward model and PPO fine-tuning
It drops direct token prediction and goes back to hidden-state matching
It trains directly on token prediction and uses training-time test so the draft consumes its own outputs during training
It removes speculative verification and samples only from the draft
questions.explanation: EAGLE-3 abandons the feature-prediction objective that limited earlier versions. It also introduces training-time test so the draft sees the same autoregressive input distribution during training that it will face at inference.

questions.question: If all N drafted tokens are accepted in one speculative step, what happens next?
options: The verifier samples one bonus token from q_(N+1)
The draft samples one bonus token from p_(N+1)
The process stops and returns control to plain decoding
All KV cache entries are discarded and rebuilt
questions.explanation: A full-accept step earns a "free" extra token from the verifier's next-position distribution. That bonus token is part of why good speculative decoding can return up to N+1 accepted tokens from one verifier forward pass.

questions.question: Why does training-time test (TTT) improve EAGLE-3 drafts?
options: It increases the verifier model's hidden size
It removes exposure bias by training the draft on its own previous predictions
It makes the draft use beam search during inference
It guarantees α = 1.0 on all tasks
questions.explanation: Naive draft training conditions on teacher-forced histories that will not exist at inference time. TTT feeds the draft its own predictions during training so train-time and test-time state distributions align more closely.
